fields.value: Study 2: How Do International Medical Students Make Sense of Internal and External Feedback to Improve Their Dutch Communication Skills?
Hao Yu - PhD Projectdata for study 2

dsDescriptionValue.value:
Summary of the Study:

This study explored how international medical students perceive and integrate internal feedback (self-reflection) and external feedback (from peers, teachers, and simulated patients) while learning medical Dutch communication skills through simulated patient consultations (SPCs).
• Design:Mixed-methods design (survey + semi-structured interviews).
• Participants: 16 third-year international medical students (3 male, 13 female; mean age = 23; all B2 Dutch CEFR level).
• Procedure: Six-session Medical Dutch course during which each session included briefing, SPC, and debriefing. Students received internal and external feedback systematically integrated into the course.
• Instruments:
o Feedback perception survey (8 items: preference, satisfaction, trustworthiness, progress facilitation).
o Semi-structured interviews (30–60 min, conducted online during COVID-19).
o Thematic analysis (Atlas.ti, data saturation reached at 16 interviews).
Key Findings:
1. Quantitative survey results:
o External feedback scored higher than internal feedback in preference, satisfaction, and trustworthiness.
o Both internal and external feedback were rated equally effective for facilitating learning progress.
2. Qualitative themes (5):
o Proactive engagement with feedback – students actively sought feedback from teachers, peers, and simulated patients, valuing clarity and actionable advice.
o Dialogue and discussion – peer/teacher discussions broadened perspectives and deepened learning.
o Self-reflection and progress tracking – internal feedback supported personal growth, even though students sometimes felt overly self-critical.
o Value from diverse perspectives – combining feedback from different sources (medical accuracy, patient empathy, peer observation) enriched understanding.
o Moment-specific and actionable feedback – timely, targeted feedback was easier to apply immediately.
3. Conclusion:
o External feedback was more trusted and satisfying, but internal feedback was critical for self-regulated learning and growth.
o Together, they formed a complementary system, fostering comprehensive communication skill development in L2 medical Dutch.
